newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa money data neutral, rate cut still viable.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa money data neutral, rate cut still viable.

text.p: May South African M3 and credit figures were broadly neutral, but the steady decline in both figures kept the country on track for a rate cut in a couple of months' time, economists said on Friday.
"These are good figures...it seems as if the downward trend is continuing," said Dawie Roodt of stockbroker Equisec.
Year-on-year broadly defined M3 money supply grew 15.40 percent in May, the Reserve Bank said, while closely-watched private sector credit annual growth fell to 16.57 percent from 17.40 in April.
The consensus forecast for M3 had been 15.19 percent and 16.56 for private credit growth.

"Obviously it would have been nicer to have had something more than this rather modest fall in growth in the credit number but it is very much a consensus outcome," said Gordon Smith of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"I would expect the rate of credit growth to decline quite sharply to about 12 percent by year-end. As long as the Reserve Bank is prepared to discount that in terms of three-month annualised rates, excluding overdrafts, then we should see a rate cut in August," he added.

A Reuters poll of 31 economists released on Thursday showed a one-point cut in South African interest rates was on the cards towards the end of the third quarter and seen as a certainty by the end of the year.
South Africa's official Bank rate currently stands at 17 percent.
Roodt said the bond market, which hit a fresh 16-month low on Friday, could take further heart from headline official gold and foreign exchange reserves due to be released next Tuesday.
Economists are looking for an increase in reserves to a new high of 24.7 billion rand against 21.8 billion in May, bolstered by income from the recent issue of bonds.
The government's R150 benchmark bond was yielding 14.31 percent in after hours dealings, virtually unchanged from the local 1400 GMT close but down nine basis points from Thursday.
